response.reasoning_text:
Durbin has loop-carried dependencies on k; inner loops can be parallelized. Fuse the z/y loops? z[i]=y[i]+alpha*y[k-i-1]; y[i]=z[i] — can fuse into y[i] = y[i] + alpha*y[k-i-1]? That changes semantics? Original: z computed from old y, then y=z. Fused: y[i] = y[i] + alpha*y[k-i-1] — but y[k-i-1] may be overwritten before use if i > k-i-1... For i where k-i-1 < i, y[k-i-1] already updated. So not safe unless careful. Keep two loops, parallelize both with nowait? Second loop depends on z from first, so no nowait between them within same parallel region... Use a single parallel region around k loop with for directives inside. Simpler: parallelize inner loops with omp for.

Provide code with #pragma omp parallel for on inner loops (schedule static). Reduction for sum.
